positions.commentary: The speaker states that investing in Carvana was very hard due to real bankruptcy risk and a lack of management credibility, making it difficult to handicap the odds in favor.
The speaker believes Google was a great value in 2019, describing it as a business that could have been bought for 'free' and noting that Bill Iren and Bill Miller discussed its value early on.
The speaker cites Bill Iren's view that Amazon is still a great value selling for 1.5 times revenue with 25% revenue growth, predicting it will double in the next three years.
The speaker mentions that HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank trade at 2.5 to 3 times book value compared to US banks at 1.5 times because their ROAs, growth, and ROEs are superior.

thesis: The episode argues that investors should focus on high-quality businesses with durable moats and disciplined management, such as Indian banks like HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, which offer significant value despite market skepticism. It also highlights that major US tech giants like Google and Amazon remain compelling long-term investments based on their historical valuations and growth trajectories.

claims.claim: The speaker states that investing in Carvana was very hard due to real bankruptcy risk and a lack of management credibility, making it difficult to handicap the odds in favor.
claims.quote: And so, at least from my perception, it would have been very hard to invest in that. Is that something not necessarily Carvana in specific, but in a situation like that where you do see so much upside, even if there is bankruptcy risks there

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that one could have bought Google in 2019 for free, citing Bill and Igren's early SOTP analysis as a key insight.
claims.quote: for example you could have bought Google in 2019 and got like GCP for kind of free right and it was just a business I was just sitting there and you know Bill and Igren basically was one of the few guys who talked about the SOTP on Google really early on

claims.claim: The speaker cites Bill Miller's view that Amazon is still a great value selling for 1.5 times revenue with 25% revenue growth, predicting it could double in three years.
claims.quote: Bill Miller really talked about Amazon and in 2016 and in one of the say and BC interviews when I was buying all the oil stocks and stuff like that Bill and Igren comes in and says Amazon to me is still a great value and I think it will double in the next three years because it still sells for 1.5 times revenue and revenues are growing 25%

claims.claim: The speaker identifies HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank as prime Indian banks with great discipline, noting they are the largest part of the portfolio due to value, despite tail risks.
claims.quote: so last year you know it's out there it's public information HDFC bank in India so so we just invest in Indian businesses as part of the pension right now so top 200 businesses in India the lowest market cap that we can buy is close to 5 billion dollars in India

claims.claim: The speaker states that HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank are the two prime banks in India with great lending discipline and management, having never had a bad year where non-performing assets surpassed previous profits.
claims.quote: so I would say you know HDFC bank Kodak Mahindra bank are the two prime banks in India with like great lending discipline and great management good government and you know they really have never had a bad year where the non performing assets you know just surpass their previous years two years profits or something like that

claims.claim: The speaker notes that HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank are growing at 13-14 percent, contradicting the market view that they are done, and they became the largest positions in the portfolio.
claims.quote: and by the way these banks are growing you know it's not like India is a growing economy faster than you know any other so these banks are still growing something like 13-14 percent and the market was basically saying they are done and I just didn't believe that and ended up making these two banks as largest positions

claims.claim: The speaker highlights that HDFC Bank is only 7 times levered, which is way lower than US book banks or other banks in India, making it a preferred choice for minimizing risk.
claims.quote: and that's why we went for the lowest leverage banks and if you look at like something like HDFC banks that's like only 7 7 times levered and that's like way lower than where the US book banks are levered or any other bank probably in India is levered

claims.claim: The speaker states that HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank trade at 2.5 to 3 times book value, compared to US banks trading at 1.5 times, due to superior ROA, growth, and ROE.
claims.quote: So so you're comfortable still basically accepting some of the balance sheet risk is some that tail risk because you feel like one there's not a lot of other opportunities that kind of present that risk reward but second you're comfortable enough with the underwriting and all that that you're okay with those as being two of your larger positions.
